module purpose: UART peripheral that services a bus: it decodes bus read/write accesses to control and data registers, provides TX and RX FIFOs, runs transmit and receive engines driven by a selected uart clock, presents status and interrupts (irq_tx_o, irq_rx_o), and supports hardware flow-control (CTS/RTS).

use-case flows.value: control register values written from the bus (enable, sim_mode, hwfc_en, prsc, baud, IRQ masks, clr_rx, clr_tx)
host write of a transmit byte into the TX FIFO (bus -> tx_fifo.wdata and tx_fifo.we)
transmit operation: tx_engine loads a FIFO byte into sreg, clocks bits out with uart_clk and drives uart_txd_o
receive operation: uart_rxd sampled into rx_engine.sreg, assembled into a byte and pushed into RX FIFO
interrupt outputs and bus-status reporting (irq_tx_o, irq_rx_o and bus_rsp_o.data status fields)
bus read returns: control/status fields or RX FIFO readback (rx_fifo.rdata -> bus_rsp_o.data) and rx_fifo.re
reset forces control registers, engine state and FIFOs to known values (rstn_i = '0' arms in processes)

conceptual assets.concept: Bus access predicates that decide which internal register or FIFO field a bus transaction addresses (strobe, read/write, addr[2])
conceptual assets.reasoning: The bus-access process reads bus_req_i.stb, bus_req_i.rw and bus_req_i.addr(2) to choose writes or reads and to route data: see the bus_access process's tests and assignments (RTL lines 176-183, 260-261, 307). The relationship map records these inputs gating the assignments: bus_req_i.addr occurrence 2 (line 178) is recorded GATES the control fields (map GATES targets include ctrl.enable), bus_req_i.rw occurrence 2 (line 177) is recorded GATES the control-data path, and bus_req_i.stb occurrence 2 (line 170) CARRIES the ack (bus_rsp_o.ack). Because these predicates directly determine where bus data lands and which reads occur, their integrity is required for correct configuration and data flow (map evidence: the cited occurrences and their GATES / CARRIES records).

conceptual assets.concept: Control-register configuration (enable, sim_mode, hwfc_en, prsc, baud, IRQ mask bits, clr_rx, clr_tx) that defines UART operating mode, clock selection, flow-control and IRQ policy
conceptual assets.reasoning: Bus writes store the configuration fields (RTL lines 176-183, 185-191); those fields are then read and used throughout the design (clkgen_en_o <= ctrl.enable at line 228; uart_clk selection at line 229; tx/rx counters load ctrl.baud at lines 349, 368, 432; fifo clears at lines 259 and 304). The map shows each control field is written from bus_req_i.data (each register has a DERIVES_FROM / CLOCKED_BY record where the receiving occurrence cites bus_req_i.data): e.g. ctrl.enable occurrence 3 (line 179) DERIVES_FROM bus_req_i.data, ctrl.prsc occurrence 3 (line 182) DERIVES_FROM bus_req_i.data, ctrl.baud occurrence 3 (line 183) DERIVES_FROM bus_req_i.data, and clr_rx/clr_tx occurrences (line 190/191) DERIVE from bus_req_i.data. These RTL lines and map records establish that these stored configuration values determine core behavior and thus require integrity.

conceptual assets.concept: Transmit data bytes (host-supplied bytes written into the TX FIFO and consumed by the transmitter to produce uart_txd_o)
conceptual assets.reasoning: A host write places an 8-bit value on tx_fifo.wdata (RTL line 260) gated by the bus write condition (tx_fifo.we at line 261). The transmitter loads FIFO data into tx_engine.sreg (RTL line 351) and shifts bits to uart_txd_o (RTL lines 365, 392). The map records the bus source-to-FIFO link (bus_req_i.data occurrence 14, line 260, SOURCES -> tx_fifo.wdata), the FIFO write-enable gating (tx_fifo.we occurrence 3, line 261, GATED_BY the bus predicates), the FIFO input signal set (tx_fifo.wdata occurrence 3, line 260, DERIVES_FROM bus_req_i.data) and the transmitter storage edge (tx_engine.sreg occurrence 3, line 351, CLOCKED_BY clk_i). The port uart_txd_o is driven by tx_engine.txd (uart_txd_o occurrence 2, line 392, COPIES tx_engine.txd). These RTL lines and map records establish the integrity property that bytes written by the bus are the exact bytes forwarded to the transmitter and out the pin.

conceptual assets.concept: Received data bytes (serial input sampled and assembled by rx_engine then stored into RX FIFO for bus readout)
conceptual assets.reasoning: The receiver samples uart_rxd_i into rx_engine.sync and shifts bits into rx_engine.sreg (RTL lines 408, 410, 434); when a byte completes rx_engine.done is asserted and rx_fifo.wdata/rx_fifo.we are used to store the byte (RTL lines 305-306). The map records uart_rxd_i occurrence 2 (line 408) CARRIES -> rx_engine.sync, rx_engine.sreg occurrence 4 (line 434) CLOCKED_BY clk_i and SOURCES rx_fifo.wdata (line 305), rx_engine.done occurrence 2 (line 306) CARRIES -> rx_fifo.we, and bus readout copies rx_fifo.rdata into bus_rsp_o.data (bus_rsp_o.data occurrence 21, line 217, COPIES rx_fifo.rdata). These RTL lines and map edges establish the integrity property that a received serial byte is the value delivered to the FIFO and presented on reads.

conceptual assets.concept: Interrupt-decision (IRQ mask bits and the irq_tx_o / irq_rx_o outputs) that reports TX/RX conditions to the system
conceptual assets.reasoning: IRQ outputs are computed from control mask bits and FIFO status: see tx_irq_generator and rx_irq_generator (RTL lines 265-273 and 310-319). The map records the mask bits written from the bus (e.g. ctrl.irq_tx_empty occurrence 3, line 188 DERIVES_FROM bus_req_i.data; ctrl.irq_rx_nempty occurrence 3, line 185 DERIVES_FROM bus_req_i.data) and the IRQ outputs driven from those fields and FIFO status (irq_tx_o occurrence 3, line 270 DERIVES_FROM ctrl.irq_tx_empty and related signals; irq_rx_o occurrence 3, line 315 DERIVES_FROM ctrl.irq_rx_nempty and rx_fifo signals). Because these decisions determine externally-observed interrupt signals, their integrity is established by the RTL lines and the cited map records.

conceptual assets.concept: Hardware flow-control policy and handshake (CTS input and RTS output) that permits or blocks transmission
conceptual assets.reasoning: The transmitter checks CTS and ctrl.hwfc_en before advancing (RTL lines 359-360) and the rtr_control process drives uart_rtsn_o depending on ctrl.hwfc_en, ctrl.enable and rx_fifo.half (RTL lines 467-477). The map records ctrl.hwfc_en written from the bus (ctrl.hwfc_en occurrence 3, line 181 DERIVES_FROM bus_req_i.data), the CTS input propagation (uart_ctsn_i occurrence 2, line 337 SOURCES -> tx_engine.cts), tx_engine.cts derived from uart_ctsn_i (tx_engine.cts occurrence 3, line 337 DERIVES_FROM uart_ctsn_i), and the RTS output gated by FIFO fullness and enable (uart_rtsn_o occurrence 3, line 475 GATED_BY includes rx_fifo.half). These RTL lines and map edges establish that flow-control settings and the CTS/RTS signals determine whether transmission proceeds, so their integrity is material to operation.

conceptual assets.concept: RX FIFO overrun flag (rx_engine.over) that records an overflow event and is reported to the bus
conceptual assets.reasoning: The fifo_overrun process sets rx_engine.over when a write occurs while the FIFO is full (RTL lines 453-461), and the value is reported on bus reads (bus_rsp_o.data includes ctrl_rx_over at line 214). The map records rx_engine.over occurrence 2 (line 214) CARRIES -> bus_rsp_o.data so the overrun bit is explicitly produced and exported: its integrity matters to correct reporting of overflow events.

conceptual assets.concept: Selected UART sampling/bit clock (uart_clk) derived from clkgen_i and ctrl.prsc that times bit sampling and shifting
conceptual assets.reasoning: The uart clock used by the TX/RX engines is selected from clkgen_i by index ctrl.prsc (RTL line 229: uart_clk <= clkgen_i(to_integer(unsigned(ctrl.prsc)))). The map records this as uart_clk occurrence 2 (line 229) SELECTED_BY ctrl.prsc and DERIVES_FROM clkgen_i. Because uart_clk gating controls baud sampling and the state machines' progress (map GATES and SELECTED_BY records at occurrences used by tx_engine and rx_engine), correctness of the selected clock (and of ctrl.prsc which sets it) is required for correct transmit/receive timing.
